name: JavaScript ES6+ Full Stack Engine Track
description: Master modern JavaScript programming from core syntax, control flow, functions, and objects to ES6+ features, closures, async Promises, DOM APIs, and application architecture.
whatYouLearn: Master JavaScript syntax, scope, and execution context
Harness ES6+ destructuring, spread, modules, and arrow functions
Manipulate arrays with map, filter, reduce, and find methods
Handle async workflows with Promises and async/await
Manipulate the DOM dynamically and respond to user events
Build a production Expense Tracker and Weather Dashboard

exercises.title: Variables, Constants & Scope (let vs const)
exercises.description: Declare block-scoped variables using let and const, avoiding var pitfalls.
exercises.theory: let and const provide block scope. Use const by default for immutable bindings, and let for reassigned counters.
exercises.objective: Declare block-scoped variables and perform arithmetic operations.
requirements: Use const for immutable product name and tax rate
Use let for final price calculation
Output formatted string with toFixed(2)
hints: const prevents variable reassignment
toFixed(2) formats numbers to two decimal places

exercises.title: Data Types & Typeof Operator
exercises.description: Identify primitives (string, number, boolean, null, undefined, symbol) vs objects.
exercises.theory: JavaScript has 7 primitive types and reference objects. Use typeof to inspect data types dynamically at runtime.
exercises.objective: Inspect variable types using the typeof operator.
requirements: Inspect string, number, and boolean types with typeof
Check array instance using Array.isArray()
hints: typeof [] returns 'object', so use Array.isArray() to test arrays

exercises.title: Functions & ES6 Arrow Functions
exercises.description: Write function declarations, expressions, and concise ES6 arrow functions.
exercises.theory: Arrow functions () => {} offer concise syntax and lexically bind the this context.
exercises.objective: Write arrow functions for mathematical calculations.
requirements: Create implicit return arrow functions add and square
Use default parameter values in calculateTotal
hints: Single expression arrow functions omit curly braces and return keyword

exercises.title: Template Literals & String Methods
exercises.description: Perform multi-line interpolation and string parsing (includes, slice, split, trim).
exercises.theory: Template literals (`${expr}`) allow variable interpolation and multi-line strings without concatenation.
exercises.objective: Parse and format user input strings.
exercises.initialCode:
let rawInput = '   user_name@domain.dev  ';
// Clean string and extract domain
requirements: Use trim() and toLowerCase() to sanitize input
Use split('@') with array destructuring
Format output using template literals
hints: trim() removes leading/trailing whitespace

exercises.title: Arrays & Essential Mutation Methods
exercises.description: Manipulate arrays using push, pop, shift, unshift, slice, and splice.
exercises.theory: Arrays store ordered item lists. push/pop add/remove from end, shift/unshift from start, and splice mutates in place.
exercises.objective: Perform array stack and queue operations.
exercises.initialCode:
let queue = ['task1', 'task2'];
// Add and remove queue elements
requirements: Use push to add item to end
Use unshift to prepend high priority item to start
Use shift to dequeue completed item
hints: shift removes and returns the first element

exercises.title: Higher-Order Iteration: map(), filter(), reduce()
exercises.description: Transform, filter, and aggregate array datasets using functional methods.
exercises.theory: Functional iteration methods do not mutate original arrays. map transforms items, filter extracts matching items, and reduce accumulates data.
exercises.objective: Calculate total revenue for active subscriptions.
requirements: Filter array for active === true
Map active objects to price numbers
Reduce price numbers to single total sum
hints: Chain filter().map().reduce() sequentially
Provide 0 as initial accumulator value in reduce
exercises.codeExample: const sum = nums.filter(n => n > 0).reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);

exercises.title: Objects, Destructuring & Optional Chaining
exercises.description: Access nested object properties cleanly using destructuring, default values, and optional chaining (?.).
exercises.theory: Destructuring unpacks object fields into variables. Optional chaining (?.) prevents runtime errors when accessing nullish nested paths.
exercises.objective: Safe extraction of nested user profile attributes.
requirements: Use object destructuring with default fallback value for role
Use optional chaining (?.) for settings path
Use nullish coalescing (??) for theme fallback
hints: ?? returns right hand side only when left hand side is null or undefined
exercises.codeExample: const { name } = user; const theme = user?.settings?.theme;

exercises.title: Object Spread & Array Rest Operators
exercises.description: Clone and merge objects and arrays using the ES6 spread operator (...).
exercises.theory: Spread operator (...) expands iterable elements. Rest operator packs remaining function arguments into an array.
exercises.objective: Immutably merge object configurations and gather rest function parameters.
requirements: Merge objects with spread operator prioritizing right-hand properties
Write rest parameter function sumAll(...numbers)
hints: Properties appearing later in object spread override earlier properties

exercises.title: Closures & Private Lexical Scope
exercises.description: Encapsulate private state using lexical closures and factory functions.
exercises.theory: A closure is a function that retains access to variables from its outer enclosing scope even after the outer function has executed.
exercises.objective: Create a counter factory function with private state.
requirements: Encapsulate private variable count inside createCounter
Return object exposing increment, decrement, and getValue methods
hints: Direct access to count variable outside function will fail, preserving privacy
exercises.codeExample: function makeAdder(x) { return y => x + y; }

exercises.title: Prototypes, Classes & OOP Inheritance
exercises.description: Write ES6 classes with constructor, methods, getters, and static members.
exercises.theory: ES6 classes provide syntactic sugar over prototype-based inheritance. Use extends and super for class inheritance.
exercises.objective: Build a User and Admin class hierarchy with inherited permissions.
requirements: Create base class User with constructor and getRole method
Create subclass AdminUser extending User with super() call
hints: super() must be called before accessing this in subclass constructors
exercises.codeExample: class Admin extends User { constructor(n) { super(n); } }

exercises.title: Asynchronous Operations & Promises
exercises.description: Create, resolve, reject, and chain asynchronous Promise instances.
exercises.theory: Promises represent future asynchronous completion or failure states (pending, fulfilled, rejected). Use .then() and .catch() to consume Promise outcomes.
exercises.objective: Simulate async database query using a Promise constructor.
requirements: Return new Promise with resolve/reject callbacks
Use setTimeout to simulate network delay
Handle resolved data with .then() and error with .catch()
hints: resolve(data) transitions promise to fulfilled state

exercises.title: Async / Await & Error Handling (try/catch)
exercises.description: Refactor Promise chains into synchronous-looking async/await blocks with try/catch/finally error handling.
exercises.theory: async functions implicitly return Promises. await pauses execution until the awaited Promise resolves, making asynchronous flow read sequentially.
exercises.objective: Write async/await functions with try/catch error boundaries.
requirements: Declare async function
Await Promise response inside try block
Include catch block and finally block
hints: await can only be used inside functions marked with async keyword
exercises.codeExample: async function get() { const res = await fetch(url); }

exercises.title: DOM Selection & Manipulation
exercises.description: Select DOM nodes using querySelector and modify text, innerHTML, styles, and classLists.
exercises.theory: The Document Object Model (DOM) provides JavaScript interfaces for reading and mutating web page elements dynamically.
exercises.objective: Select DOM elements and update content and CSS class states.
exercises.initialCode: // Select element and update inner content
requirements: Select element using querySelector('#id')
Update textContent property
Add class using classList.add() and modify style
hints: textContent is safer than innerHTML as it avoids XSS vulnerabilities

exercises.title: DOM Event Listeners & Event Delegation
exercises.description: Attach addEventListener handlers and leverage event delegation for dynamic list items.
exercises.theory: Event delegation binds a single listener on a parent container to handle events from present or future child elements via event.target.
exercises.objective: Implement an event delegation handler on a dynamic list container.
exercises.initialCode:
const container = document.querySelector('#list');
// Attach delegated click listener
requirements: Use addEventListener('click', handler)
Check target matching class using event.target.matches()
Remove item node using closest('li').remove()
hints: closest() traverses parent nodes to locate matching element selector

exercises.title: Fetch API & HTTP REST Integration
exercises.description: Perform HTTP GET and POST requests using the native Fetch API.
exercises.theory: fetch() sends HTTP requests and returns a Promise resolving to a Response object. Parse JSON payloads using response.json().
exercises.objective: Send a POST JSON payload using fetch API.
requirements: Send fetch request with method: 'POST'
Include Content-Type: application/json header
Check response.ok before parsing response.json()
hints: JSON.stringify() converts JavaScript objects to JSON string payloads
exercises.codeExample: const res = await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(data) });

exercises.title: Browser Storage (localStorage & sessionStorage)
exercises.description: Persist and retrieve JSON data structures across browser sessions using localStorage.
exercises.theory: localStorage stores key-value pairs persistently across page reloads. Values must be stored as strings using JSON.stringify.
exercises.objective: Persist and retrieve user preferences object from localStorage.
exercises.initialCode:
const preferences = { theme: 'dark', fontSize: 16 };
// Save and load preferences from localStorage
requirements: Use localStorage.setItem with JSON.stringify
Use localStorage.getItem with JSON.parse and fallback default
hints: Always wrap JSON.parse in try/catch or nullish check to prevent parse errors

exercises.title: ES Modules (import / export)
exercises.description: Structure modular codebase files using named and default ES module exports.
exercises.theory: ES Modules allow splitting code across files. Use export for named exports and export default for primary file exports.
exercises.objective: Write modular utility export and import structures.
exercises.initialCode: // Export helper functions
requirements: Demonstrate named exports syntax for helper functions
Demonstrate default export syntax
hints: Named exports must be imported using curly braces import { add } from './math.js'

exercises.title: Debounce & Throttle Optimization
exercises.description: Optimize high-frequency event handlers (search inputs, window resizing) using debouncing.
exercises.theory: Debouncing delays function execution until a specified delay has elapsed since the last time the event was triggered.
exercises.objective: Build a reusable debounce utility function for search inputs.
requirements: Create debounce wrapper taking function and delay ms
Clear active timerId with clearTimeout
Re-assign timerId using setTimeout
hints: clearTimeout cancels pending execution when new events fire in rapid succession

exercises.title: Custom Event Emitter Architecture
exercises.description: Build an event bus (pub/sub pattern) supporting on, off, and emit methods.
exercises.theory: The Publisher/Subscriber (Event Emitter) pattern decouples components by enabling them to publish and listen for named event notifications.
exercises.objective: Implement a simple EventEmitter class.
requirements: Create EventEmitter class with events dictionary
Implement on(event, listener) subscriber method
Implement emit(event, data) publisher method
hints: Store listeners in an array keyed by event name

exercises.title: Capstone Project: Interactive Expense Tracker App
exercises.description: Build a complete client-side Expense Tracker application featuring balance calculations, transaction additions, array filtering, and localStorage persistence.
exercises.theory: This capstone exercise unifies core ES6+ topics: array higher-order methods, object modeling, DOM manipulation, event handling, and localStorage state persistence.
exercises.objective: Engineer a complete Expense Tracker application module.
requirements: Store transactions list with unique ID, text, and amount
Calculate total balance, positive income, and negative expenses
Persist and load transactions using localStorage
hints: Filter positive amounts for income and negative amounts for expenses
exercises.codeExample: const balance = txs.reduce((a, t) => a + t.amount, 0);
